issues: BLOCKER: The revert script (`write_revert`) can abort before it finishes. It extracts the tar, which puts back the old common-* files, and then runs `pam-auth-update --disable ... --enable unix` with no `--force` under `set -e`. pam-auth-update records md5sums of the files it generates. The tar-restored common-* no longer match them, so it can refuse as 'locally modified' and exit non-zero. The script then dies before it removes the added profiles and drop-ins, restores chage, and runs `faillock --user aj --reset`. That breaks the auto-timer, the Rollback section and PASTE 3 together. Fix: put `faillock --user aj --reset || true` right after the tar extract. Run pam-auth-update with `--force` and treat a failure as non-fatal (`|| echo WARN-pam-auth-update`). Still do the rm and chage steps. After the restore, check that common-auth has neither `pam_faillock` nor `nullok`-less unix.

BLOCKER: PASTE 3, the KVM recovery, runs as `sudo bash ~/cis-audit/batch-9.sh 3`. It is meant for when sudo or PAM is broken, so it needs the very thing that may have failed. It also depends on the .sh file and on `pam-auth-update` working. Fix: add a sudo-free fallback to PASTE 3 and the `## Rollback` section. It would be a `# RUNS ON: JOHNNY (KVM)` block, run from a root shell (root console login or `su -`). Its commands: `tar -C / -xzf /root/batch9-pam-security.tar`, then `faillock --user aj --reset`, then `systemctl stop johnny-cis-batch9-revert.timer`. State plainly that the raw tar restore alone returns a working stock PAM stack. Keep the script form as the first choice.

Nit: `sudo -n -v` in PASTE 1 and PASTE 2 runs as root, so it always succeeds and proves nothing about aj's sudo. The real test is PASTE 2 being started with `sudo bash` through the new stack from a new session. The docs already say this for PASTE 2. Do not describe PASTE 1's check as an aj sudo check.

Nit: confirm on Johnny that `pam-auth-update --disable A B C --enable X Y Z` accepts multiple names per option and both options together. Check `man pam-auth-update` before the run. If it fails, PASTE 1 reverts automatically, so this is not a safety problem.

Nit: `active_bare` exits on STOP-value without calling the revert when CHANGED=1. Nothing in PAM has changed at that point, so it is harmless, but it is inconsistent with the other helpers. PASTE 2 could also check that the timer is inactive after `systemctl stop`.

Nit: `TMOUT=900` is readonly in a login shell. It will drop idle SSH sessions after 15 minutes. That is expected for CIS 5.4.3.2, but AJ should know before relying on long-lived sessions. 5.4.1.1 sets aging only for aj and `useradd -D`. Root and other users with passwords are not covered, and the re-audit may still flag them.
